_comment: Example watchlist for poller.sh / pr-watch-poller.sh. Copy to $HOME/.config/run-issues/watchlist.json and replace every <placeholder>. Lookup order: RUN_ISSUES_WATCHLIST if set (and then it is the ONLY candidate — a missing file is an error, never a fallback), else $HOME/.config/run-issues/watchlist.json, else the legacy $HOME/dotfiles/machine-studio/run-issues-watchlist.json. JSON has no comment syntax — the _comment key is the convention used instead. LABEL SEMANTICS: `labels` (per repo, falling back to `default_labels`) are ANDed — an issue must carry EVERY listed label to be picked up. Listing `auto-clean`, `waiting` or `wip` here silently disables pickup for that repo: the pick query already excludes all three, so requiring one of them yields zero matches forever, with no error and no log line. See README section 6.2. OPTIONAL KEY `pr_watch_max_concurrent` (number, top-level): a separate concurrency cap for pr-watch-poller.sh only; when omitted it falls back to global_max_concurrent, so leaving it out keeps the current behaviour exactly. Because PR scans are seconds of work (unlike the tens-of-minutes orchestrator runs), raising it lets the PR watcher reach the whole watchlist faster without widening poller.sh's orchestrator concurrency. The env var PR_WATCH_GLOBAL_MAX overrides it. See CLAUDE.md section 7.

repos._comment: Multi-remote form: one clone polling two orgs. Both labels are required on the issue (AND), so this entry picks up only issues carrying BOTH auto-run and backend — narrow the scope, never widen it.
